mechanism.cells: Autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells modified ex vivo using a WAS-encoding lentiviral vector

primary_evidence.population: 27 male patients with severe WAS, ages 0.98-35.1 years
primary_evidence.design: Two open-label single-arm studies plus expanded access; historical within-patient pretreatment comparison
primary_evidence.outcomes: Survival, severe infections, moderate/severe bleeding; WASP expression and hematopoietic biomarkers
primary_evidence.limitation: No contemporaneous control; small and selected population; no BUB1B/MVA or muscle compensation efficacy endpoints

primary_endpoints: Annualized severe infection rate, months 6-18 versus pretreatment year
Annualized moderate/severe bleeding rate, first year versus pretreatment year

primary_evidence.summary: Original 2019 nonrandomized phase 1/2 interim analysis: eight treated boys with WAS; sustained corrected HSPC engraftment and increased WASP-positive blood cells; 100% survival at median 3.6 years. These are WAS outcomes.
Original 2013 first-three-patient report: WASP-expression engraftment with platelet and immune improvement after WAS-directed HSPC gene therapy.

transfer_assessment.inference: The actual approved product adds WAS, not BUB1B, and the studied outcomes are hematopoietic/immune. Its efficacy cannot be transferred to BUB1B restoration, mosaic variegated aneuploidy, or muscle compensation from these records. A BUB1B-engineered product would be a separate intervention requiring its own evidence.
transfer_assessment.do_not_promote: Generic lentiviral/HSPC platform feasibility is not evidence for this product treating MVA.
